title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-09-23
content:
Attendees: Aisha (PM), Tom, Lucas, Priya, Mei
Date: 2026-09-23

Summary:
- Focus this week on kernel memory fragmentation fixes, stabilized KV-cache eviction policy, and tuning batching heuristics for short/long-tail workloads.
- We shipped kernel patch v0.9.3 to staging; saw 6-8% p50 latency regression on 8k sequence long-run (investigating).
- KV-cache: experimental ttl-based eviction landed behind flag; initial throughput +5% for prefix-heavy traffic.
- Batching: introduced dynamic batch size floor to avoid small-batch overhead during tail traffic; trying two schedulers (EDF-like vs time-window).

Standups / Progress:
- Kernel (Tom):
  - Merged urban/frag-fix PR (GH: redwood/serving-runtime#1419) addressing slab reuse; reduced per-request malloc churn in microbenchmarks.
  - Discovered p50 regressions in 8k seq tests on A100 machines after enabling vectorized attention kernels; probable trade-off between kernel launch overhead and in-kernel memory copies. Profiled with perf and nvprof; collecting traces for longer runs.
  - Next: revert one micro-optimization in vectorized path and re-run long-seq job; consider hybrid path selection based on seq_len threshold.

- KV-cache (Lucas):
  - Deployed ttl-eviction prototype to canary (flag: kv.ttl_eviction=true). Observed 5% increase in throughput and 3% drop in token-cost for demo traffic (high prefix reuse).
  - Edge-case: clients with highly dynamic prefixes causing cache churn -> eviction thrash. Added soft-rail: exempt entries referenced >N times in last T minutes.
  - Working on metrics to expose hit-rate by prefix-length and by model to prioritise caching heuristics per model family.
  - Next: push metrics to console dashboards and start A/B test vs current LRU for two customer routes.

- Batching (Priya):
  - Implemented dynamic floor: min_batch_size = max(2, observed_qps * 0.02) for SLOs to avoid inefficient single-request batches at low QPS.
  - Evaluated two schedulers:
    - EDF-window: schedules by request deadline, slightly better 95p latency for latency-sensitive routes.
    - Time-window: simpler, better throughput on bursty traffic but worse 95p.
  - Running a week-long replay test with production trace; early results: time-window increases throughput by ~7% for large-batch workloads, EDF reduces 95p by ~9% for chat workloads.
  - Next: expose per-route policy config, defaulting to EDF for chat and time-window for high-throughput batch inference.

Blockers / Risks:
- Kernel regression on long sequences is highest priority; if not resolved we may need to gate the vectorized kernel rollout. Risk: performance rollback for models with >4k context.
- KV eviction thrash could increase p99 latency for rare-tail requests; need more conservative heuristics before broad rollout.
- Batching policy complexity: config surface increases; ops needs per-route safety defaults to avoid dangerous configs in Dedicated customers.

Metrics / Observations:
- Staging perf runs (8k seq) before patch: p50=180ms, p95=480ms; after patch p50=192ms, p95=500ms. Microbenchmarks (2k seq) improved p50 by ~4%.
- KV-cache canary route: hit-rate from 18% -> 34% on prefix-heavy trace; miss penalty reduced ~12%.
- Batching simulation: average batch size up from 9.4 -> 11.8 on replay with time-window, CPU utilization +6%.

Action Items:
- Tom: run hybrid kernel-selection A/B (vectorized vs fallback) for seq_len buckets (<=2k, 2k-6k, >6k). Target: A/B results by 2026-09-27.
- Lucas: add per-model caching metrics to console and start two-week A/B on SERV-beta routes. Target dashboard by 2026-09-28.
- Priya: land per-route batching policy + safety defaults; doc PR for ops config. Target PR + canary 2026-09-29.
- Aisha: coordinate with SRE to add safety alert if p99 increases >15% after kernel/kv/batching changes.

Notes / Misc:
- Customer ask (from PROTO team): lower tail-latency for model-m family on Dedicated. Recommend enabling EDF batching + cache tuning; schedule follow-up workshop next week.
- Planning: propose to include kernel rollback plan in runbook for 1.0 kernel rollout.
- Meeting next week: deep-dive on long-seq profiling (invite: kernel, perf, SRE, infra).

Raw links / refs: GH PRs: redwood/serving-runtime#1419, #1427. Jira: SERV-884 (kv eviction), SERV-892 (batching config). Confluence: INFRA-KV-CACHE-PLAYBOOK (draft).

Notes to self: keep artifacts from perf runs (nvprof traces) attached to SERV-892 ticket.
summary: Weekly serving-runtime update: kernel memory fixes merged, investigating long-seq latency regression; ttl-based KV eviction shows promise in canary; batching scheduler experiments (EDF vs time-window) with per-route policy planned. Action items assigned for A/B tests and dashboards.
